queries.title: Employee directory with department, designation and manager
queries.sql:
SELECT e.emp_id,
       e.first_name || ' ' || e.last_name AS employee,
       d.dept_name,
       g.title AS designation,
       m.first_name || ' ' || m.last_name AS manager,
       e.status
  FROM employee e
  JOIN department  d ON d.dept_id  = e.dept_id
  JOIN designation g ON g.desig_id = e.desig_id
  LEFT JOIN employee m ON m.emp_id = e.reports_to
 ORDER BY e.emp_id

queries.title: Head-count and average basic salary of every department (including empty ones)
queries.sql:
SELECT d.dept_name,
       d.location,
       COUNT(e.emp_id) AS active_employees,
       ROUND(AVG(g.basic_salary), 2) AS avg_basic_salary
  FROM department d
  LEFT JOIN employee e    ON e.dept_id = d.dept_id AND e.status = 'Active'
  LEFT JOIN designation g ON g.desig_id = e.desig_id
 GROUP BY d.dept_id, d.dept_name, d.location
 ORDER BY active_employees DESC, d.dept_name

queries.title: Employees whose basic salary is above the company average
queries.sql:
SELECT e.emp_id,
       e.first_name || ' ' || e.last_name AS employee,
       g.title,
       g.basic_salary
  FROM employee e
  JOIN designation g ON g.desig_id = e.desig_id
 WHERE e.status = 'Active'
   AND g.basic_salary > (SELECT AVG(g2.basic_salary)
                           FROM employee e2
                           JOIN designation g2 ON g2.desig_id = e2.desig_id
                          WHERE e2.status = 'Active')
 ORDER BY g.basic_salary DESC

queries.title: Department-wise salary cost for the latest payroll month
queries.sql:
WITH latest AS (
    SELECT pay_month, pay_year
      FROM payroll
     ORDER BY pay_year DESC, pay_month DESC
     LIMIT 1
)
SELECT d.dept_name,
       COUNT(*)              AS employees_paid,
       SUM(p.gross_salary)   AS total_gross,
       SUM(p.total_deductions) AS total_deductions,
       SUM(p.net_salary)     AS total_net
  FROM payroll p
  JOIN latest l     ON l.pay_month = p.pay_month AND l.pay_year = p.pay_year
  JOIN employee e   ON e.emp_id = p.emp_id
  JOIN department d ON d.dept_id = e.dept_id
 GROUP BY d.dept_name
 ORDER BY total_net DESC

queries.title: Top 5 earners by net salary in the latest month (with rank)
queries.sql:
WITH latest AS (
    SELECT pay_month, pay_year
      FROM payroll
     ORDER BY pay_year DESC, pay_month DESC
     LIMIT 1
)
SELECT RANK() OVER (ORDER BY p.net_salary DESC) AS rank,
       e.first_name || ' ' || e.last_name AS employee,
       g.title,
       p.net_salary
  FROM payroll p
  JOIN latest l      ON l.pay_month = p.pay_month AND l.pay_year = p.pay_year
  JOIN employee e    ON e.emp_id = p.emp_id
  JOIN designation g ON g.desig_id = e.desig_id
 ORDER BY p.net_salary DESC
 LIMIT 5

queries.title: Attendance summary of every employee for September 2026
queries.sql:
SELECT e.emp_id,
       e.first_name || ' ' || e.last_name AS employee,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE a.status = 'Present')  AS present,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE a.status = 'Half-Day') AS half_days,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE a.status = 'Absent')   AS absent,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE a.status = 'Leave')    AS on_leave
  FROM employee e
  JOIN attendance a ON a.emp_id = e.emp_id
 WHERE a.att_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-09-01' AND DATE '2026-09-30'
 GROUP BY e.emp_id, e.first_name, e.last_name
 ORDER BY absent DESC, half_days DESC, e.emp_id

queries.title: Employees who lost pay (LOP) in any month, with the amount lost
queries.sql:
SELECT p.pay_month,
       p.pay_year,
       e.first_name || ' ' || e.last_name AS employee,
       p.lop_days,
       ROUND(p.basic_salary / p.working_days * p.lop_days, 2) AS basic_lost
  FROM payroll p
  JOIN employee e ON e.emp_id = p.emp_id
 WHERE p.lop_days > 0
 ORDER BY p.pay_year, p.pay_month, basic_lost DESC

queries.title: Remaining 2026 leave balance of every active employee
queries.sql:
SELECT e.emp_id,
       e.first_name || ' ' || e.last_name AS employee,
       g.annual_leave_quota AS quota,
       fn_leave_balance(e.emp_id, 2026) AS balance
  FROM employee e
  JOIN designation g ON g.desig_id = e.desig_id
 WHERE e.status = 'Active'
 ORDER BY balance, e.emp_id

queries.title: Pending leave requests and the manager who must approve them
queries.sql:
SELECT lr.leave_id,
       e.first_name || ' ' || e.last_name AS employee,
       lr.leave_type,
       lr.start_date,
       lr.end_date,
       (lr.end_date - lr.start_date + 1) AS calendar_days,
       COALESCE(m.first_name || ' ' || m.last_name, '(Admin)') AS approver
  FROM leave_request lr
  JOIN employee e      ON e.emp_id = lr.emp_id
  LEFT JOIN employee m ON m.emp_id = e.reports_to
 WHERE lr.status = 'Pending'
 ORDER BY lr.start_date

queries.title: Managers with at least 3 direct reports
queries.sql:
SELECT m.emp_id,
       m.first_name || ' ' || m.last_name AS manager,
       COUNT(e.emp_id) AS direct_reports
  FROM employee m
  JOIN employee e ON e.reports_to = m.emp_id AND e.status = 'Active'
 GROUP BY m.emp_id, m.first_name, m.last_name
HAVING COUNT(e.emp_id) >= 3
 ORDER BY direct_reports DESC

queries.title: Itemised payslip lines of every employee for the latest month
queries.sql:
WITH latest AS (
    SELECT pay_month, pay_year
      FROM payroll
     ORDER BY pay_year DESC, pay_month DESC
     LIMIT 1
)
SELECT e.emp_id,
       e.first_name || ' ' || e.last_name AS employee,
       c.component_type,
       c.component_name,
       pd.amount
  FROM payroll p
  JOIN latest l           ON l.pay_month = p.pay_month AND l.pay_year = p.pay_year
  JOIN employee e         ON e.emp_id = p.emp_id
  JOIN payroll_detail pd  ON pd.payroll_id = p.payroll_id
  JOIN salary_component c ON c.component_id = pd.component_id
 ORDER BY e.emp_id, c.component_type, pd.amount DESC

queries.title: Active employees who have not taken any approved leave in 2026
queries.sql:
SELECT e.emp_id,
       e.first_name || ' ' || e.last_name AS employee,
       d.dept_name
  FROM employee e
  JOIN department d ON d.dept_id = e.dept_id
 WHERE e.status = 'Active'
   AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1
                     FROM leave_request lr
                    WHERE lr.emp_id = e.emp_id
                      AND lr.status = 'Approved'
                      AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM lr.start_date) = 2026)
 ORDER BY e.emp_id

queries.title: Month-by-month payroll totals and payment status
queries.sql:
SELECT pay_year,
       pay_month,
       COUNT(*) AS payslips,
       SUM(gross_salary) AS total_gross,
       SUM(net_salary)   AS total_net,
       CASE WHEN BOOL_AND(status = 'Paid') THEN 'All paid'
            ELSE COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status <> 'Paid') || ' unpaid' END AS payment_status
  FROM payroll
 GROUP BY pay_year, pay_month
 ORDER BY pay_year, pay_month

queries.title: Departments whose average net salary is above the company average (latest month)
queries.sql:
WITH latest AS (
    SELECT pay_month, pay_year
      FROM payroll
     ORDER BY pay_year DESC, pay_month DESC
     LIMIT 1
)
SELECT d.dept_name,
       ROUND(AVG(p.net_salary), 2) AS avg_net_salary
  FROM payroll p
  JOIN latest l     ON l.pay_month = p.pay_month AND l.pay_year = p.pay_year
  JOIN employee e   ON e.emp_id = p.emp_id
  JOIN department d ON d.dept_id = e.dept_id
 GROUP BY d.dept_name
HAVING AVG(p.net_salary) > (SELECT AVG(p2.net_salary)
                              FROM payroll p2
                              JOIN latest l2 ON l2.pay_month = p2.pay_month AND l2.pay_year = p2.pay_year)
 ORDER BY avg_net_salary DESC

queries.title: Age and tenure of every active employee (derived attributes)
queries.sql:
SELECT e.emp_id,
       e.first_name || ' ' || e.last_name AS employee,
       EXTRACT(YEAR FROM AGE(CURRENT_DATE, e.dob))::INT AS age,
       e.date_of_joining,
       EXTRACT(YEAR FROM AGE(CURRENT_DATE, e.date_of_joining))::INT AS years_of_service
  FROM employee e
 WHERE e.status = 'Active'
 ORDER BY years_of_service DESC, e.emp_id

queries.title: Total paid out per salary component in the latest month
queries.sql:
WITH latest AS (
    SELECT pay_month, pay_year
      FROM payroll
     ORDER BY pay_year DESC, pay_month DESC
     LIMIT 1
),
lines AS (
    SELECT c.component_type, c.component_name, pd.amount
      FROM payroll p
      JOIN latest l           ON l.pay_month = p.pay_month AND l.pay_year = p.pay_year
      JOIN payroll_detail pd  ON pd.payroll_id = p.payroll_id
      JOIN salary_component c ON c.component_id = pd.component_id
)
SELECT component_type, component_name, SUM(amount) AS total
  FROM lines
 GROUP BY component_type, component_name
UNION ALL
SELECT component_type, '— TOTAL ' || UPPER(component_type) || 'S', SUM(amount)
  FROM lines
 GROUP BY component_type
 ORDER BY component_type, total

queries.title: Employees who were both absent and on approved leave in September
queries.sql:
SELECT e.emp_id, e.first_name || ' ' || e.last_name AS employee
  FROM employee e
  JOIN attendance a ON a.emp_id = e.emp_id
 WHERE a.status IN ('Absent', 'Half-Day')
   AND a.att_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-09-01' AND DATE '2026-09-30'
INTERSECT
SELECT e.emp_id, e.first_name || ' ' || e.last_name
  FROM employee e
  JOIN leave_request lr ON lr.emp_id = e.emp_id
 WHERE lr.status = 'Approved'
   AND lr.start_date <= DATE '2026-09-30' AND lr.end_date >= DATE '2026-09-01'
 ORDER BY emp_id

queries.title: Everyone with leadership responsibility: department heads or people managers
queries.sql:
SELECT e.emp_id, e.first_name || ' ' || e.last_name AS employee, 'Department head' AS responsibility
  FROM employee e
 WHERE e.emp_id IN (SELECT head_emp_id FROM department WHERE head_emp_id IS NOT NULL)
UNION
SELECT m.emp_id, m.first_name || ' ' || m.last_name, 'People manager'
  FROM employee m
 WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM employee e WHERE e.reports_to = m.emp_id AND e.status = 'Active')
 ORDER BY emp_id, responsibility

queries.title: Employees who checked in after 09:35 more than 10 times since August
queries.sql:
SELECT e.emp_id,
       e.first_name || ' ' || e.last_name AS employee,
       COUNT(*) AS late_days,
       MAX(a.check_in) AS latest_check_in
  FROM attendance a
  JOIN employee e ON e.emp_id = a.emp_id
 WHERE a.check_in > TIME '09:35'
 GROUP BY e.emp_id, e.first_name, e.last_name
HAVING COUNT(*) > 10
 ORDER BY late_days DESC

dml.title: UPDATE: annual salary revision of a designation
dml.sql:
UPDATE designation
   SET basic_salary = basic_salary * 1.10
 WHERE title = 'Software Engineer'
RETURNING desig_id, title, basic_salary;
dml.note: Future payroll runs use the new basic; paid payslips keep their stored snapshot.

dml.title: UPDATE: deactivate a salary component
dml.sql:
UPDATE salary_component
   SET is_active = FALSE
 WHERE component_name = 'Internet Allowance'
RETURNING component_id, component_name, is_active;
dml.note: Inactive components are skipped by generate_monthly_payroll.
